Create solution from prioritization

Source: R/method_Solution.R
create_solution_from_prioritization.Rd

Create a new solution based on spatial prioritization.

Usage

create_solution_from_prioritization(
  name,
  project,
  prioritization,
  settings,
  column = NULL,
  metrics = NULL,
  id = uuid::UUIDgenerate()
)

Arguments

name

character value with the name.

project

new_project() object to which prioritization should be added.

prioritization

numeric vector with a value for each planning unit to indicate zone allocations. For example, if the prioritization has three zones, then elements with values ranging between 1 and 3 correspond to planning units that are locked to the three zones (respectively). Additionally, elements with values ranging between 4 and 6 correspond to planning units that are selected as a priority for the three zones (respectively).

settings

list of settings used to generate the solution.

column

character value with column name used to store prioritization in the dataset that underpins project.

metrics

list with evaluation metrics for prioritization. Defaults to NULL such that the metrics are calculated automatically.

id

character value with unique identifier. Defaults to a random identifier (uuid::UUIDgenerate()).

Value

A new_solution() object.

Settings format

The argument to settings must be a list with the following elements.

"features"

A data.frame with the theme and feature settings. These are used to specify the targets and weights considered for the features during optimization. Each row corresponds to a different feature, and it must have the following columns: "id", "name", "column", "zone", "target", and "weight". Note that target values must be expressed as a proportion (i.e., value between zero and one).

"locks"

A data.frame with the settings to specify which locks are used to lock in planning units to a particular zone. Each row corresponds to a different lock, and it must have the following columns: "id", "name", "column", "zone", and "priority".

"costs"

A data.frame with the cost settings. These are used to specify which costs are considered for each zone. Each row corresponds to a different cost, and it must have the following columns: "id", "name", "zone", and "weight".

"zones"

A data.frame with settings for the multi-objective optimization. Each row corresponds to a different zone, and it must have the following columns: "name" and "weight".

See also

Other functions for calling class methods: create_dataset_from_sf(), create_legend(), create_solution(), create_solution_legend(), create_tile_from_file(), create_tile_from_project(), create_tile_from_sf(), new_dataset(), tool_generated_provenance()

Examples

# simulate data
p <- simulate_project()
s <- simulate_prioritization_settings(p)
d <- solve_prioritization(p, s, gap = 0.1)

# generate solution
x <- create_solution_from_prioritization(
  name = "sol",
  project = p,
  prioritization = d,
  settings = s
)

# print solution
print(x)
#> A <Solution> object.
#> • name: "sol"
#> • id: "81257b7b-ab9b-4e37-b71d-2790ec9b4258"
#> • settings: <list> object
